title: Starting up a project: the eight activities and outputs
blurb: Name the eight activities of starting up a project, what each produces and who is involved in the appointments.
question: In which activity of starting up a project is the project product description created, and which activity creates the lessons log?

teach.body: Formally: starting up a project has eight activities, from appointing the executive and project manager to requesting project initiation. In plain English: get the leaders in place, learn from the past, sketch the case and the product, build the team, choose how to do the work, pull it together in a brief, plan initiation, then ask the board for the go-ahead.

teach.body: In 'prepare the outline business case', the project manager consults the senior user, senior supplier and executive to define what the project will deliver and creates the project product description. The outline business case is only a high-level view at this point; it gives an agreed foundation for the more detailed business case developed in initiating a project.

items: Select the project approach: decide how the work will be done, for example in-house or by third parties, build or buy, and which delivery method.
Plan the initiation stage: initiation takes time and resources, so plan it and have it approved so it is not aimless.
Request project initiation: formally ask the board for authority to initiate, presenting the project approach, the team appointments and the initiation stage activities and controls.

values: Set up the daily log; gather lessons
Define the project approach; develop the PPD
Identify an initial set of key risks

teach.body: Larkfield Building Society's business layer appoints Helen Price as executive, and Helen appoints Kwame Asante as project manager. Kwame opens a lessons log and talks to the team that ran the last system migration. He consults Helen and the senior user and supplier to draft the outline business case and project product description. The approach is to buy a package. He assembles the brief, plans a six-week initiation and requests initiation, presenting approach, appointments and initiation plan.

teach.text: Classic traps: the project manager is NOT involved in appointing the project management team (business layer accountable, executive responsible). The initiation stage plan is made in starting up a project, NOT in managing a stage boundary. A verbal pitch is not a complete request: starting up is not finished without the initiation stage plan.

items: Eight activities: appoint executive and PM; assess previous lessons; prepare outline business case; appoint PMT; select project approach; assemble project brief; plan initiation stage; request project initiation.
Lessons log from assessing previous lessons; PPD with the outline business case.
Business layer accountable and executive responsible for appointments.
The request presents approach, appointments and initiation activities and controls.

summary: You can now list the eight activities of starting up a project, the product each creates and who is accountable and responsible for the appointments. You can also say which practices are applied and what a complete request for initiation contains.

A.q: Which activity of starting up a project creates the lessons log?
options: Assess previous lessons
Appoint the project management team
Plan the initiation stage
Assemble the project brief
A.why: Assess previous lessons creates the lessons log and draws on people and teams with experience of similar projects (13.4.2).

whyNot.1: Appointing the team produces the PMT structure and role descriptions.
whyNot.2: Planning the initiation stage produces the initiation stage plan.
whyNot.3: Assembling the brief draws together the outputs of earlier activities into the project brief.

A.q: In which activity of starting up a project is the project product description created?
options: Select the project approach
Assemble the project brief
Prepare the outline business case
Appoint the project management team
A.why: In prepare the outline business case the PM consults the senior user, senior supplier and executive to define what will be delivered and creates the PPD (13.4.3).

whyNot.0: Selecting the project approach decides how the work will be done, not what the project product is.
whyNot.1: The brief includes the PPD, but the PPD is created earlier, alongside the outline business case.
whyNot.3: Appointing the team sets up roles; it does not define the project product.

A.q: Which is the last activity of starting up a project?
options: Assemble the project brief
Request project initiation
Plan the initiation stage
Authorize initiation
A.why: Starting up ends with request project initiation, in which the PM formally asks the board for authority to initiate (13.4.8).

whyNot.0: Assembling the brief comes before planning the initiation stage and making the request.
whyNot.2: Planning the initiation stage comes just before the request; the request completes the process.
whyNot.3: Authorize initiation is a directing a project activity carried out by the board in response.

B.q:
Which two statements about appointments in starting up a project are correct?
1. The business layer is accountable for appointing the executive and project manager.
2. The project manager is responsible for appointing the project management team.
3. The executive is responsible for appointing the project management team.
4. Project assurance is accountable for appointing the project manager.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: The business layer is accountable for both appointment activities (1), and the executive is responsible for appointing the team (3) (13.6, tab 13.2).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: the project manager is not involved in appointing the project management team.
whyNot.2: Both are false: the PM is not involved in appointing the team, and assurance is not involved in appointing the PM.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the business layer, not project assurance, is accountable for appointing the PM.

B.q: During 'prepare the outline business case', whom does the project manager consult to define what the project will deliver?
options: The business layer, team managers and support
Project assurance, project support and users
The change authority and the team managers
The senior user, senior supplier and executive
B.why: The PM consults the senior user, senior supplier and executive to define what the project will deliver and create the PPD (13.4.3).

whyNot.0: Team managers and project support are not the people who define what the project will deliver.
whyNot.1: Assurance and support are not named as those consulted to define the project product.
whyNot.2: A change authority deals with requests for change later; team managers are engaged through work packages.

B.q: Which question is addressed in the 'select the project approach' activity?
options: Will the work be done in-house or by third parties?
Who will be accountable for the project's success?
Which lessons from earlier projects apply here?
How long will the initiation stage take?
B.why: Selecting the project approach asks how the work will be approached, such as in-house or third party, build or buy, and the delivery method (13.4.5).

whyNot.1: Accountability for success is settled by appointing the executive.
whyNot.2: Earlier lessons are the subject of assess previous lessons.
whyNot.3: The length of initiation is settled in plan the initiation stage.

C.q: Which activity produces the initiation stage plan, and which process prepares the plans for later delivery stages?
options: Plan the initiation stage; initiating a project
Assemble the project brief; controlling a stage
Plan the initiation stage; managing a stage boundary
Request project initiation; managing a stage boundary
C.why: The initiation stage plan comes from 'plan the initiation stage' in starting up; every later stage plan is prepared in managing a stage boundary near the end of the previous stage.

whyNot.0: The first part is right, but initiating a project prepares the project plan, not the delivery stage plans.
whyNot.1: The brief does not contain the initiation stage plan, and controlling a stage does not prepare stage plans.
whyNot.3: The request presents the initiation plan but does not create it.

C.q: A project manager tells the board verbally why the project is worth initiating, but no initiation stage plan exists yet. Is starting up a project complete, and why?
options: Yes, because a verbal briefing is enough to request initiation
No, because the request must include the initiation stage plan
No, because the full business case has not been approved yet
Yes, because the board will plan the initiation stage itself
C.why: Starting up a project is not complete without the initiation stage plan; the request presents the approach, appointments and initiation activities and controls (13.4.8).

whyNot.0: A verbal explanation is common, but the formal request still needs the initiation stage plan behind it.
whyNot.2: The full business case is prepared in initiating a project, so it is not needed before initiation.
whyNot.3: The board approves the initiation stage plan; the project manager prepares it in starting up.

C.q: Which practice is applied in starting up a project when the project manager sets up the daily log and gathers lessons from previous projects?
options: Plans
Quality
Risk
Progress
C.why: Tab 13.3 lists setting up the daily log and gathering lessons under the progress practice.

whyNot.0: Plans is applied by defining the project approach and developing the project product description.
whyNot.1: Quality is applied by understanding the quality expectations and requirements.
whyNot.2: Risk is applied by identifying an initial set of key risks.

reteach.title: One line per activity
reteach.question: Can you tell the story of starting up a project in eight short lines?

blocks.body: Someone must own it (executive) and run it (PM). What went wrong or right before? (lessons). Why do it and what is it? (outline business case and PPD). Who else steers it? (the team). How will we do it? (approach). Write it down (brief). Plan the next step (initiation stage plan). Ask permission (request initiation).

items.label: Appoint the executive and the PM

blocks.text: The board's 'authorize initiation' is NOT one of the eight: it belongs to directing a project and responds to the request.

explain.body: First the executive and the project manager are appointed; the PM runs the project day to day on the executive's behalf. Later the rest of the project management team is appointed to reflect business, user and supplier interests. The business layer is accountable and the executive responsible for both.

test.q: In 'appoint the executive and the project manager', why is a project manager appointed?
options: To run the project day to day for the executive
To provide independent assurance to the board
To represent the users who will benefit
To approve the outline business case
test.why: Appointing a PM allows the project to be managed day to day on behalf of the executive (13.4.1).

whyNot.1: Project assurance is the board's responsibility and cannot be done by the PM.
whyNot.2: Representing users is the senior user's role.
whyNot.3: The PM prepares the outline business case; the executive is accountable for it.

explain.body: Assess previous lessons creates the lessons log by consulting people and teams with experience of similar projects and reviewing lessons reports. Prepare the outline business case gives a high-level justification and creates the project product description.

explain.h: From the past to the case

test.q: Which statement about the outline business case is correct?
options: It is the detailed version used to authorize the project
It is written after the project plan is approved
It is a high-level view that initiation develops further
It is prepared by team managers for the board
test.why: The outline business case is only a high-level view and is the foundation for the detailed business case developed in initiating a project (13.4.3).

whyNot.0: The detailed (full) business case, prepared in initiation, is used when authorizing the project.
whyNot.1: The project plan is prepared later, in initiating a project.
whyNot.3: The project manager prepares it, with the executive accountable; team managers are not involved.

explain.body: Select the project approach decides how the work will be done: in-house or third party, build or buy, and the delivery method. Assemble the project brief then pulls the earlier outputs together into a firm, shared starting point for initiation.

test.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The project [?], assembled in starting up a project, gives a firm, shared starting point for initiation.
options: mandate
brief
plan
approach
test.why: The project brief, assembled in starting up a project, provides a well-defined starting point and a firm foundation for initiation.

whyNot.0: The mandate is the trigger supplied by the business layer, not something assembled in starting up.
whyNot.2: The project plan is prepared in initiating a project.
whyNot.3: The project approach is one input to the brief, not the assembled starting point itself.

explain.body: Plan the initiation stage, because initiation takes time and resources and must not be aimless. Then request project initiation: formally ask the board for authority to initiate, presenting the project approach, the team appointments and the initiation stage activities and controls.

test.q: What does the project manager present when requesting project initiation?
options: The project plan, full business case and tolerances
The PID with all nine management approaches
Work package descriptions and team plans
The approach, appointments and initiation plan
test.why: The request presents the project approach, the project management team appointments and the initiation stage activities and controls (13.4.8).

whyNot.0: The project plan and full business case are prepared during initiation, after this request.
whyNot.1: The PID and management approaches are assembled in initiating a project.
whyNot.2: Work packages and team plans belong to delivery stages.
